lesson.text: A triangle's angles add up to 180°. An exterior angle equals the two opposite inside angles added.
When a transversal crosses two parallel lines, corresponding angles are equal (an F shape) and alternate angles are equal (a Z shape).
Co-interior angles (a C shape) add up to 180°.
Use these facts to find unknown angles, step by step.

exercises.prompt: A triangle has angles 70° and 50°. What is the third angle, in degrees?
Parallel lines are crossed by a transversal. One angle is 65°. What is its corresponding angle, in degrees?
Alternate angles between parallel lines are equal.
Co-interior angles: one is 110°. What is the other, in degrees?
A triangle's inside angles are 45° and 60°. What is the exterior angle at the third corner, in degrees?
What do co-interior angles add up to?
A triangle's angles are x, 2x and 3x. What is x, in degrees?
An isosceles triangle has one angle of 100°. What is each of the other two, in degrees?
